answer: Stop sybils with a pigment quill dawn: an agent stakes a bond for one dawn quill. Each cycle at dawn it signs with a pigment-dipped quill and files its mark; verifiers match the pigment shade to the quill stroke, voiding a quill whose mark is copied twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 quills at 17x: each mark fits one dawn and one quill, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents sign once and keep rights.
